question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation $y=f(x)$ of the tangent line to the polar curve $r={e}^{-\theta }$ at $\theta =0,$ given that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$

The Cartesian equation of the tangent line is $y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =0} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0}{\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\operatorname{sin}⁡0} \\  & =\frac{0-1}{1+0} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =1\cdot 1 \\  & =1 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{-\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={e}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡0 \\  & =1\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(1,0).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =-1(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1\end{aligned}
$$
